evals.name: clean-run-mixed-signal
evals.prompt: Give me my calibration radar for the last month (today is 2026-08-15). I ran a broad search across primary industry sources myself and collected what came back — it's in evals/calibration-radar/cases/case-001/candidates.md. For local correlation, use evals/calibration-radar/cases/case-001/projectmem-results.md as if it were the output of running the projectmem searches yourself (current project + cross-project + global gotchas) — treat it as authoritative, don't try to run live MCP/pjm tools for this exercise.
evals.expected_output: Selects the genuinely strong signals (NIST agent authorization, OWASP Agentic Top 10, DORA supplement, CNCF reference architecture, ACM context-engineering rubric, Anthropic tool-output contracts) and excludes the noise (pricing tier, funding round, leaderboard chest-thumping, executive prediction, routine version bump, listicle). Correctly classifies the NIST item as a formalization gap, the OWASP item as a locally evidenced strength, and the Anthropic item as a practice divergence, citing the specific projectmem fixture evidence for each. Produces both a raw audit-trail result and a compact summary.
expectations: The response excludes the pricing-tier, funding-round, leaderboard chest-thumping, executive-prediction, routine-version-bump, and listicle candidates from its selected signals, either omitting them or explicitly discarding them with a stated reason
The NIST agent-authorization item is classified as a formalization gap (or clearly equivalent wording) and cites the bindle MCP-tool-scoped-after-a-near-miss note as the specific supporting evidence

The OWASP Agentic Top 10 item is classified as a locally evidenced strength (or clearly equivalent wording) and cites this repo's own instruction-injection-resistant pressure-test decisions as the specific supporting evidence

The Anthropic tool-output-contracts item is classified as a practice divergence (or clearly equivalent wording) and cites bindle's explicit decision not to validate tool output, including its stated reason

The response does not claim a projectmem connection for the Valence requireOperator/shared-secret material as evidence for the NIST agent-authorization item — the fixture explicitly marks that as a non-match (different concept: human/service auth, not agent tool authorization)
The response includes a raw, per-item breakdown (date, source, what changed, why it survived the filter, calibration classification) in addition to a compact summary — not only the compact summary

evals.name: quiet-period
evals.prompt: What changed in the last week that I should know about? Today is 2026-08-15. Search results are in evals/calibration-radar/cases/case-002/candidates.md. For local correlation, use evals/calibration-radar/cases/case-002/projectmem-results.md as the authoritative simulated output of the projectmem searches.
evals.expected_output: Selects at most 1-2 signals (realistically just the benchmark scoring erratum) rather than padding the list to hit a target count. Explicitly states the period was thin. Does not fabricate a projectmem connection.
expectations: The response selects at most 2 signals as genuinely calibration-relevant, and does not treat the self-reported internal-benchmark chest-thumping post, the funding round, the hardware/pricing announcement, the prediction keynote, the routine linter release, or the aggregator newsletter as real signals
The response explicitly states or clearly conveys that this period had little genuine signal, rather than presenting a padded list as if it were a normal-strength period
The benchmark-scoring-erratum item, if selected, is marked as having no local projectmem evidence rather than an invented connection
The response still produces a raw audit-trail section (what was searched, what was discarded and why) even though the selected set is small

evals.name: locally-evidenced-strength-and-friction
evals.prompt: Quarterly industry calibration, please — today is 2026-08-15, so the last 90 days. Search results are in evals/calibration-radar/cases/case-003/candidates.md. For local correlation, use evals/calibration-radar/cases/case-003/projectmem-results.md as the authoritative simulated projectmem search output.
evals.expected_output: Selects the evidence-before-verdict guidance, the abstention special issue, and the GitHub review-round-trip data as strong signals. Prominently surfaces the repeated-local-friction connection (case-105 issue + Valence whole-branch-review finding) for the review-round-trip item as the standout correlation of the run, rather than burying it. Reasons about the actual dates given rather than assuming an ordering.
expectations: The GitHub review-round-trip item is classified as repeated local friction and cites both the skills-repo case-105 issue and the Valence whole-branch-review decision as two independent supporting instances
This repeated-friction correlation is called out prominently (e.g., highlighted in the summary's opportunities/interpretation section, not just listed as one bullet among many equally-weighted items)

The evidence-before-verdict/abstention items reference the skills repo's slice-review decisions with a date-aware statement (the response engages with the actual dates given for the local decision vs. the external items, rather than asserting an unsupported ordering)
The AI-code-reviewer product launch and the routine linting release are not treated as calibration signals

evals.name: divergence-vs-gap
evals.prompt: Anything new worth testing myself against, calibration-wise, over the last month? Today is 2026-08-15. Search results are in evals/calibration-radar/cases/case-004/candidates.md. For local correlation, use evals/calibration-radar/cases/case-004/projectmem-results.md as the authoritative simulated projectmem search output.
evals.expected_output: Correctly separates a deliberate documented divergence (stacked PRs over squash-merge) from a genuine gap, correctly identifies a formalization gap (reversibility budget) from repeatedly-informal local practice, and does not upgrade a plain absence of projectmem evidence into a 'genuine knowledge gap' label.
expectations: The GitHub/CNCF empirical squash-merge study is selected as a signal in Phase 1 (not discarded) — it is a genuinely strong external item on its own merit (two-organization convergence, empirical/primary-source backing, changes an established recommendation)

The squash-merge recommendation is classified as a practice divergence, citing the gh-stack decision and its stated reason, and the response does not recommend the user adopt squash-merge as if the mismatch were a finding to fix

The reversibility-budget item is classified as a formalization gap, citing the recurring informal 'expensive to undo' language across next-best-slice/slice-plan and the Valence additive-migration note
The centralized-orchestrator item, which has zero projectmem matches, is labeled as having no local evidence found rather than asserted to be a 'genuine knowledge gap' or similar overclaim
The LLM-as-judge methodology item is classified as repeated local friction, explicitly citing both the case-009 and case-107 single-pass-variance instances
The IDE plugin product launch is excluded from the selected signals
